**Pre / Post Test — Data Analysis and Report Writing TOT
Data for Health (D4H) Initiative**

Name: ________________________________     Country team: ____________________     Date: __________
*Circle the letter of the SINGLE best answer for questions 1–25 (2 marks each). Answer questions 26–27 in the space provided (10 marks each). Total: 70 marks. Time allowed: 60 minutes.*

**1. [D4H project basics]  ** The Data for Health (D4H) Initiative is supported by:

**A.  ** The World Bank

**B.  ** Bloomberg Philanthropies

**C.  ** The Global Fund

**D.  ** USAID

**2. [D4H project basics]  ** The implementing partner for this Training of Trainers course is:

**A.  ** The World Health Organization

**B.  ** UNICEF

**C.  ** The CDC Foundation

**D.  ** The Carter Center

**3. [Equity principles]  ** In data analysis, applying an equity lens primarily means:

**A.  ** Collecting more data overall

**B.  ** Disaggregating results to reveal differences between population groups

**C.  ** Publishing only national averages

**D.  ** Removing outliers from the dataset

**4. [Equity principles]  ** Which disaggregation is the MINIMUM expected for an equity-sensitive program report?

**A.  ** Sex, age group, and geography (e.g., district)

**B.  ** Facility ownership type only

**C.  ** Urban/rural only

**D.  ** No disaggregation is needed if the national average meets the target

**5. [Analysis objectives]  ** A well-written analysis objective should be:

**A.  ** Broad, so it covers everything

**B.  ** Specific, answerable with available data, and linked to a decision

**C.  ** Focused only on data collection methods

**D.  ** Written after the analysis is finished

**6. [Analysis objectives]  ** Which is the best-written analysis objective?

**A.  ** To analyze TB data

**B.  ** To estimate TB treatment success rates by district for 2021–2024 cohorts and compare them against the 90% national target

**C.  ** To learn more about tuberculosis

**D.  ** To collect TB data from districts

**7. [Data cleaning]  ** The FIRST step after receiving a dataset from the data custodian should be to:

**A.  ** Start building charts immediately

**B.  ** Verify record counts against the release note and run data-quality checks

**C.  ** Delete all records with any missing value

**D.  ** Share the file with colleagues for their input

**8. [Data cleaning]  ** A district reports more treatment successes than patients registered in its cohort (success count > cohort size). This is a problem of:

**A.  ** Completeness

**B.  ** Timeliness

**C.  ** Validity

**D.  ** Confidentiality

**9. [Combining datasets]  ** When merging a TB case file with a district population file, the essential requirement is:

**A.  ** Both files have the same number of rows

**B.  ** A common join key present in both files (e.g., district_code)

**C.  ** Both files are sorted alphabetically

**D.  ** Both files were created in the same software

**10. [Census rates]  ** The TB notification rate per 100,000 population is calculated as:

**A.  ** (Population ÷ notified cases) × 100,000

**B.  ** (Notified cases ÷ mid-year population) × 100,000

**C.  ** (Notified cases × 100,000) − population

**D.  ** Notified cases ÷ 100,000

**11. [Census rates]  ** Rates using population denominators are preferred over raw case counts when comparing districts because:

**A.  ** Rates are always larger numbers

**B.  ** Districts have different population sizes, so counts alone are misleading

**C.  ** Counts cannot be put in tables

**D.  ** Donors prefer rates

**12. [Descriptive statistics]  ** For a strongly skewed distribution (a few districts with very high values), the most appropriate measure of the typical value is the:

**A.  ** Mean

**B.  ** Median

**C.  ** Maximum

**D.  ** Sum

**13. [Pivot tables]  ** In Excel, a pivot table is best used to:

**A.  ** Write report paragraphs

**B.  ** Summarize data by categories — e.g., total cases by district and year

**C.  ** Create maps

**D.  ** Send emails

**14. [Data quality]  ** Data 'completeness' in routine surveillance most directly refers to:

**A.  ** The percentage of expected reports actually received

**B.  ** How fast reports arrive

**C.  ** Whether values fall in valid ranges

**D.  ** How recent the data are

**15. [IMRAD]  ** In the IMRAD report structure, the correct order of sections is:

**A.  ** Introduction, Results, Methods, Discussion

**B.  ** Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion

**C.  ** Methods, Discussion, Results, Introduction

**D.  ** Results, Introduction, Discussion, Methods

**16. [IMRAD]  ** Interpretation of findings ('what the results mean') belongs in the:

**A.  ** Results section

**B.  ** Methods section

**C.  ** Discussion section

**D.  ** Title

**17. [Table best practices]  ** Every table in a program report must have:

**A.  ** A number, a self-contained title (what/where/when), units, and a source footnote

**B.  ** At least 10 columns

**C.  ** Color shading on every other row

**D.  ** A 3D border

**18. [Table best practices]  ** Which is the best table title?

**A.  ** TB data

**B.  ** Table 1. Notified TB cases by district, Demoland (fictional), 2021 and 2025

**C.  ** Numbers

**D.  ** Table showing various TB-related information for consideration

**19. [Figure best practices]  ** When charting case counts over time, the y-axis should normally:

**A.  ** Start at zero so the visual change is honest

**B.  ** Start just below the lowest value to 'zoom in'

**C.  ** Use a different scale for each year

**D.  ** Be omitted to reduce clutter

**20. [Figure best practices]  ** The most appropriate chart for showing a trend over five years is a:

**A.  ** Pie chart

**B.  ** Line chart

**C.  ** 3D exploded pie chart

**D.  ** Word cloud

**21. [Maps]  ** When mapping disease burden across districts, you should map:

**A.  ** Raw case counts, because they are simplest

**B.  ** Rates per population, so districts of different sizes can be compared fairly

**C.  ** Only the capital district

**D.  ** Facility names

**22. [Report templates]  ** The abstract of a report should be written:

**A.  ** First, to guide the writing

**B.  ** Last, after the rest of the report is final

**C.  ** By the data custodian

**D.  ** Only for academic journals

**23. [Recommendations]  ** Which is a well-written recommendation?

**A.  ** More efforts should be made to improve TB control

**B.  ** The National TB Program should deploy a mobile X-ray screening team to Westbrook district by Q3 2027, aiming to screen 5,000 high-risk adults

**C.  ** TB is a serious problem

**D.  ** Districts should try harder

**24. [Recommendations]  ** Every recommendation in a report should be:

**A.  ** Linked to a specific finding presented in the report

**B.  ** Kept vague so nobody is held accountable

**C.  ** At least two pages long

**D.  ** Written only for international audiences

**25. [Training methodologies]  ** Adult learners generally learn best when training:

**A.  ** Is 100% lecture with no interaction

**B.  ** Builds on their experience and includes hands-on practice

**C.  ** Has no breaks

**D.  ** Covers as many topics as possible as fast as possible
